newsitem.title: USA: Molten Metal posts disappointing Q1.
newsitem.headline: Molten Metal posts disappointing Q1.

text.p: Molten Metal Technology Inc posted first quarter earnings early on Thursday morning that came in well below analysts' estimates.
Molten lost $1.00 a share for the quarter compared to a loss of just a penny last year. Analysts had been expecting a loss of $0.35 a share, according to First Call.
The environmental technology company cited a decrease in construction and research and development from "M4", its joint venture with Lockheed Martin as hurting its revenues.

Revenues fell sharply, to $5.0 million from $22.4 million in the first quarter last year. The Waltham, Massachusetts company also cited the completion of a U.S. Department of Energy demonstration program for the revenue shortfall.
It said it plans to restructure the Lockheed Martin venture but expects to incur equity losses until completion of the restructuring, due in the second quarter.

As part of the previously-announced restructuring, the company restated its 1996 fourth quarter results, including a one-time non-cash charge related to a write-down of M4 assets triggered by the pending M4 restructuring. It noted that no long-lived assets were impaired.
Shares of Molten Metal closed at 6-7/8 on Wednesday.

The stock price is a far cry from its 1996 levels, when the shares traded for about $30 until October, when the stock was sliced nearly in half, to about 14, after it said it expected third and fourth quarter losses after a funding cut by the U.S. Department of Energy.
The stock has steadily eroded since then to its current levels, hurt by new of a shareholder lawsuit and a forecast of losses for the first half of 1997.
